bib.title: In Search of Needles in a 11M Haystack: Recurrent Memory Finds What LLMs Miss

read.skipped: Figure 9 (main RMT/RMT-R results) is an image; its numbers are not in the text layer, so they are not recorded.

question: How well do GPT-4-Turbo, Mistral, RAG and a recurrent-memory GPT-2 find and reason over facts hidden in very long distractor text?
hypothesis: Recurrent memory excels at filtering out irrelevant information compared to relying solely on attention; attention-based LLMs use only part of their long window.
contributions: BABILong, a generative benchmark for processing arbitrarily long documents with distributed facts
Evaluation of GPT-4 and RAG on needle-in-a-haystack QA up to millions of tokens
Evaluation of a recurrent memory transformer on inputs up to 11 million tokens

method.summary: BABILong hides bAbI task sentences inside PG19 book text, padded sentence by sentence to a target length. GPT-4-Turbo, Mistral and GPT-4+RAG are prompted; GPT-2 with Recurrent Memory Transformer (RMT) and a self-retrieval variant (RMT-R) is fine-tuned per task with curriculum on up to 32 segments.
method.task: synthetic multi-fact question answering in long distractor context (bAbI qa1-qa10)

datasets.name: BABILong (bAbI qa1-qa10 hidden in PG19)
datasets.size: 10000 train and 1000 test samples per task; 2 to 320 facts per sample depending on task
datasets.split: train 10000 / eval 1000 per task; 10M-token eval on first 100 samples only
datasets.source: bAbI (Weston et al., 2016) facts, background PG19 (Rae et al., 2020); Wikipedia embeddings used in one RAG test
datasets.preprocessing: Background sentences added in natural order until target length reached

models.name: RMT and RMT-R (GPT-2 backbone)
models.architecture: GPT-2 decoder with recurrent memory tokens; RMT-R adds single-head cross-attention over all past memory states

training.steps: {5000, 10000} with early stopping if metrics stop increasing
training.seq_len: curriculum: RMT 1-2-4-6-8-16-32 segments, RMT-R 2-4-6-8-16-32; per stage n, segments sampled from 1 to n; segment 512 tokens
training.hardware: up to 4 Nvidia A100 80Gb per experiment

other.seed_note: seed for background text fixed for test set, not fixed in training

inference.samples: Fig 3, 4, 5: averages of 25 samples; RAG (Fig 6): 50 samples per length per task; RMT: full 1000-sample test set up to 1M tokens, first 100 for 10M
inference.prompting: Task description, 2 to 3 examples in <example> tags, context in <context> tags, question duplicated with QUESTION mark, output format instruction (Appendix B)
inference.retrieval: FAISS via Langchain, text-embedding-ada-002; chunking by NLTK sentences or 512-token segments; top 5 chunks; GPT-4-Turbo reads retrieved facts

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: percent of BABILong questions answered correctly

metrics.name: retrieval accuracy (top 5)
metrics.definition: binary: relevant fact(s) present in the top 5 retrieved chunks

eval.protocol: Single run per setting; no significance tests stated

prompts.purpose: qa1 prompt for GPT-4-Turbo and Mistral
prompts.text:
I will give you context with the facts about positions of different persons hidden in some random text and a question. You need to answer the question based only on the information from the facts. If a person was in different locations, use the latest location to answer the question.
<example>...</example>
<context>
{qa1 query with noise}
</context>
QUESTION: {qa1 question}
Always return your answer in the following format: The most recent location of 'person' is 'location'. Do not write anything else after that.
prompts.where: Appendix B (qa2-qa5 prompts also given there)

results.claim: GPT-4-Turbo fails needle tasks for most of its 128K window.
results.setup: BABILong qa1-qa5, GPT-4-Turbo 128K, 0k to 128k, 25 samples per cell
results.quote: GPT-4 fails to solve needle in a haystack tasks for 75
results.note: Figure 3 caption: fails for 75 % of available context window; per-cell values only in figure.

results.claim: Conclusion says GPT-4 and RAG rely heavily on the first 25 percent of the input.
results.setup: GPT-4-Turbo qa1 with facts placed in input quarters (Fig 11)
results.quote: Their performance heavily relies on the first 25 % of the input,
results.note: Appendix C instead says the hardest location is the middle (depth = 50); the two statements are not reconciled.

results.claim: Facts in the middle of context are hardest for GPT-4-Turbo to find.
results.setup: GPT-4-Turbo qa1, all facts in same quarter of input, 4k to 64k
results.quote: The most difficult location to identify the facts is in the middle of context which corresponds to the depts = 50 in the Fig. 11.

results.claim: RAG with sentence chunks beats 512-token chunks on retrieval; sentence retrieval falls notably only at 10M tokens.
results.setup: qa1, ada-002 embeddings, FAISS, top 5, PG19 background
results.quote: with a notable decrease in accuracy observed only at the 10M token context

results.claim: RAG fails on qa2 and qa3, which need two or three supporting facts, because the second fact is not similar to the question.
results.setup: qa2-qa10 vector retrieval, sentence vs 512-token chunks
results.quote: both methods were unsuccessful in tasks 'qa2' and 'qa3'

results.claim: RMT and RMT-R trained at about 16k tokens keep performance out to 128k with marginal degradation and beat GPT-4.
results.setup: GPT-2 137M with RMT/RMT-R, 32 segments of 512 tokens training, per-task models
results.note: Per-length accuracies are in Fig 9 (image), not in the text.

results.claim: Recurrent models still beat RAG at 1M and 10M tokens, over 600 times the training length.
results.setup: RMT/RMT-R vs GPT-4 RAG, qa1-qa5, up to 10M tokens

results.claim: Fine-tuning GPT-3.5 on 100 qa1 samples helps at 16k but accuracy still falls as noise grows.
results.setup: GPT-3.5, 100 qa1 tasks of 16k tokens, 3 epochs

results.claim: RMT evaluation time grows linearly with context: 315 minutes per 1000 samples at 1M tokens on one A100.
results.setup: RMT, single A100 80Gb, includes data processing
results.table: Table 2, column 1M, row PROCESSING TIME, MINUTES

limits: Only PG19 and Wikipedia used as background; similar-fact interference could make it harder
Retrieval component not optimised (only OpenAI embeddings) and GPT-4/Mistral prompts may be suboptimal
Tasks are simple algorithmic bAbI tasks, chosen intentionally
RMT models are trained per task with a small GPT-2; RMT-R storage grows linearly with segments; RMT has finite storage
Main RMT results are in an image (Fig 9); 10M-token evaluation uses only 100 samples
No seeds, decoding settings or temperature stated for GPT-4/Mistral; RAG fails partly because default retrieval ignores temporal order

terms.definition: Benchmark that hides sentences of a bAbI task between sentences of irrelevant PG19 text to reach a desired length

lineage.note: adds self-retrieval over past memory states

lineage.work: Scaling transformer to 1M tokens and beyond with RMT (Bulatov et al., 2023)

figures.caption: RMT and RMT-R significantly outperform LLMs with and without retrieval on extremely long needle in a haystack tasks.
